summary: Returns the value as an integer, or throws.
description: A number with no fractional part. Nothing is coerced, so the string `"42"` is not an integer, and `NaN` is not either.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as an integer.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not an integer.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireInteger(42); // => 42
requireInteger(-7); // => -7
requireInteger(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireInteger(NaN); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
